# schema.py
*`src/pySEA/rayTEM/schema.py`*

Column naming schema for rayTEM microscopes.

The vocabulary was reverse-engineered from names already in the repo rather
than invented: `examples/01_basicRays.ipynb` already used `PL1`, `PD1_a` and
`PSa`/`PSb`. The last two were `Quadrapole` objects standing in for a stigmator
pair, which is why `S` first meant stigmator.

**`S` is a sextupole since 2026-10-27** (Eric: "quads are for stigmation; use S
for sextupoles"). A quadrupole is `Q` whether it focuses or stigmates, so the
notebook's pair is now `PQa`/`PQb`, and a `Quadrapole` named with `S` is reported
with `Q` as the letter to use. rayTEM has no `Sextupole` element yet: `S` maps to
the class name `Sextupole`, which nothing matches until one is added, so an `S`
name on a plain `Element` placeholder is accepted and on any typed class is an
error.

Two deliberate non-choices, both load-bearing:

- **No new attribute.** The schema reads `name` only, so `section["CL1"]`
  lookup ([assemblies.md](assemblies.md)), `.sea` round-trips and every
  existing microscope definition keep working with no migration.
- **`Element.kind` is untouched.** `kind` is consumed by
  `MicroscopeSection.__init__` (`ignoreLensThickness`) and `__delitem__` in
  [assemblies.md](assemblies.md); it describes the transfer matrix, not the
  position in the column. Reusing it for section/role would change ray
  propagation.

Consumed by sea-pearl's `MicroscopeModel`, which inherits `validate_schema`
from `Microscope` and so needs no code of its own. sea-pearl's
`instrument-control-model-builder` skill requires a clean report before a
model is bound to a backend.

## Module-level functions

### `section_code(name)` *(line 388)*
Resolve a section name to its schema code.

Returning `None` is not an error: it marks the section *unmanaged*, and
`validate_section` then skips its elements entirely. That is what keeps ad-hoc
scopes (`MicroscopeSection(name="sec1")`) valid under `strict=True`. The cost
is that a typo'd section name silently disables checking for everything inside
it — `validate_microscope` reports it as `info` for exactly this reason.

### `parse_element_name(name)` *(line 417)*
Parse an element name into its schema parts.

Index and axis are both optional and independent: `PSa` has an axis but no
index, `CL1` the reverse, and `CD1a` is the winding `a` of the condenser's
first dipole. The regex is built from `AXIS_SUFFIXES` rather than `\w+` — an
open suffix would make `CLs` parse as a condenser lens. An older underscore
(`PD1_a`) still parses.

A multipole is named on its own in its section, never on the lens it sits by
(Eric, 2026-10-21). The retired attached form (`CL1_D1a`) no longer parses;
`validate_element_name` recognises it only to name what to write instead
(`CD1a`). Numbers count each type within a section in column order: gaps
are allowed (`GD1`, `GD2`, `GD3`, `GD10`), going backwards is an error, and
they are the schema's own, not a controller's slot numbers.

### `migrate_legacy_section(section)`
The spectrometer was `S` until 2026-10-21 and is `E` now. A section named
`S` is renamed `E` as it is read (`seashells.SEASerializable.from_hdf5_group`,
which every read passes through, rayTEM's and sea-pearl's), and its elements
named on the old code (`SP1`) follow (`EP1`). There is no `S` alias.

### `element_type_codes_for(element)` *(line 531)*
Return the type codes an element's class may legitimately carry.

Matches against the whole MRO, not `type(x).__name__`. That is what lets
sea-pearl's `LensModel` satisfy `L` through its `Lens` base, and it is why
`StageModel`/`ScanCoilModel` (which derive from plain `Element`) come back
empty and are never name-checked.

### `validate_section(section, code, strict, prefix)` *(line 742)*
Validate one microscope section against the schema.

Validation is scoped by section, so this is the real entry point: an
unmanaged section returns early and its elements are never examined.
Duplicate-name checking runs first and applies in every case, since ambiguous
names break `section[name]` lookup regardless of schema.

Note the two-stage exemption in the element loop. A class in
`NAME_REQUIRED_CLASSES` must carry a parseable name; any other class (`Drift`,
`Source`) is skipped *only if its name does not parse*, so `sample` and `VOA`
stay valid while a `Drift` named `PV1` is still held to the schema.

### `validate_microscope(scope, strict)` *(line 830)*
Validate a whole microscope against the column naming schema.

Calls `validate_section(..., strict=False)` per section and applies the
`strict` policy once at the end, so a strict run reports every finding in the
column instead of raising on the first. Intra-section duplicates are left to
`validate_section`; this function adds only the cross-section case, which is
what breaks `microscope[name]`.

### `register_section(code, name, aliases, container)` *(line 875)*
Add a section code to the vocabulary.

Mutates module-level state and rebuilds the element regex. There is no
unregister — tests that call it must snapshot and restore the vocabulary (see
the `vocabulary` fixture in [tests/test_schema.md](tests/test_schema.md)).
The intended use is a column region this schema does not ship, such as a Wien
filter. `register_element_type` takes a `required` flag for the rarer case of
a code that only *permits* a name, the way `V` does for `Drift`.

### `describe_schema()` *(line 956)*
Return a printable summary of the current vocabulary.

Prose for a person or a prompt. Agents that need to *act* on the vocabulary
should read `get_schema_vocabulary()` instead.

### `get_schema_vocabulary()` *(line 1108)*
Return the current vocabulary as plain JSON-serialisable data.

The structured twin of `describe_schema()`: `sections` (code, name, aliases),
`element_types` (code, description, classes, `name_required`),
`axis_suffixes`, `patterns` (one, `element`: `<SECTION><TYPE>[INDEX][AXIS]`),
`retired` (forms that no longer validate, each with the name to write
instead: `CL1_D1a` -> `CD1a`, `SP1` -> `EP1`), `name_regex`,
`name_required_classes`, `exempt_classes` and `rules` (including
own-section multipoles and column-order numbers). Rebuilt from the module
constants on every call, so `register_section` / `register_element_type`
additions show up — but only in the process that registered them.

sea-pearl's MCP server serves it as `sea_pearl_get_naming_schema` and checks
names with `validate_microscope` as `sea_pearl_validate_names`; that is what
the builder skill reads instead of a hand-copied table. A site code
registered in an agent's own Python process is invisible to the MCP server's
process unless it is registered at import time there too.

`exempt_classes` is `Drift` (under `V`, which never requires a name) plus the
untyped `Element` and `Source` (the private `_UNTYPED_CLASSES`, since no
constant otherwise names them). Classes outside every type code (`Gun`,
`AberrationScreen`) are exempt as well; the `rules` entry says so rather than
enumerating every class.

## SchemaIssue *(class · line 240)*
A single schema finding.

Severity is the whole contract: only `"error"` fails validation. `"info"`
records something a reader should know — an unmanaged section, a container
section, a schema-typed element with no name — without failing a strict run.
Adding a new check means deciding which of the two it is.
